title: Serology Protocol for Antigen Detection
author: Dr. John Smith
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bewejfbe

steps.title: Prepare Samples and Standards
steps.instruction: Prepare samples and standard protein dilutions using the standard diluent.

substeps.instruction: If sample antigen concentration potentially exceeds the highest point of the standard curve (> 1,000 pg/ml), prepare one or more dilutions using the standard diluent.
Prepare standard curve concentrations (typically 0 to 1000 pg/ml, but up to 3000 pg/ml) using two-fold or three-fold dilutions of the stock solution with standard diluent.
Use fresh tips after each dilution when preparing serial dilutions of the protein standard.

steps.title: Coat Plate with Capture Antibody
steps.instruction: Dilute the capture antibody to the appropriate concentration and add to the plate.

substeps.instruction: Ensure sufficient volume for 50-100 ul per well.
Add the diluted capture antibody to the plate, cover, and incubate for 2 hours at room temperature (RT).

steps.title: Wash Plate
steps.instruction: Wash the plate to remove unbound capture antibody.

substeps.instruction: Remove the solution.
Wash with 200 ul per well wash buffer for 3 x 5 minutes on a shaking platform.

steps.title: Block Plate
steps.instruction: Block the plate to prevent non-specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 ul blocking buffer per well.
Cover the plate and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature (RT), or alternatively block overnight at 4uC.

steps.title: Incubate Samples and Standards
steps.instruction: Add prepared samples and standards to the plate.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the volume per well is the same as the capture antibody used in the coating step.
Remove the blocking buffer and add the samples and standards.
Cover the plate and incubate for 1 hour at RT.

steps.title: Wash Plate
steps.instruction: Wash the plate to remove unbound samples and standards.

substeps.instruction: Remove the solution.
Wash with 200 ul per well wash buffer for 3 x 5 minutes on a shaking platform.

steps.title: Add Detection Antibody
steps.instruction: Dilute and add the biotinylated detection antibody to the plate.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the biotinylated detection antibody to the appropriate concentration, using the same volume per well as the capture antibody.
Add the diluted detection antibody to the plate, cover, and incubate for 1 hour at RT.

steps.title: Wash Plate
steps.instruction: Wash the plate to remove unbound detection antibody.

substeps.instruction: Remove the solution.
Wash with 200 ul per well wash buffer for 3 x 5 minutes on a shaking platform.

steps.title: Add Enzyme Conjugate
steps.instruction: Dilute and add the enzyme conjugate to the plate.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the enzyme conjugate to the appropriate concentration, using the same volume per well as the capture antibody.
Add the diluted enzyme conjugate to the plate, cover, and incubate for 1 hour at RT.

steps.title: Wash Plate
steps.instruction: Wash the plate to remove unbound enzyme conjugate.

substeps.instruction: Remove the solution.
Wash with 200 ul per well wash buffer for 6 x 5 minutes on a shaking platform.

steps.title: Develop Signal
steps.instruction: Add substrate and incubate to develop color.

substeps.instruction: Add substrate solution to the plate using the same volume per well as the capture antibody.
Incubate the plate at RT until the desired color intensity is reached (ideally a clear gradient for standards).

steps.title: Stop Reaction and Measure
steps.instruction: Stop the enzymatic reaction and measure the absorbance.

substeps.instruction: Stop the reaction by adding an equal amount of stop solution.
If using TMB, measure the absorbance at 450 nm; otherwise, use the appropriate detection technique for the substrate used.
